title: Siemens Data Center Push Makes Skeleton Latest Baltic Unicorn
key_facts: Siemens bought into Skeleton Technologies, an Estonian maker of energy storage systems, valuing it at more than $1 billion, its CEO said.
The deal closed this month and was worth more than $100 million; the exact figure was not given.
Siemens gets exclusive rights to sell Skeleton's high-power storage to data centers, said Siemens technology chief Peter Koerte.
The systems smooth sudden swings in data center power use; CEO Taavi Madiberk says up to 40% more computing can be had if power is managed well.
Skeleton plans to spend over $200 million on US growth including factories; Bloomberg reported in March it aims for a US listing next year.
The two firms already worked together on a €220 million plant near Leipzig, Germany.
quote_evidence: Siemens has bought into Skeleton Technologies, an Estonian maker of energy storage systems.
In return, Siemens can sell Skeleton’s high-power storage systems to data centres, and no one else can.
why_it_matters_hint: Shows industrial groups paying for equipment that keeps AI data centers supplied with steady power.
notes: Bloomberg original blocked. Quotes in TNW come from Bloomberg and Skeleton's CEO; 40% claim is the CEO's.
